## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

Let me plan the game: "CRIE UM JOGO MOBILE DE PIXELS BONITO E INTERATIVO DE FAROESTE" = Create a beautiful and interactive mobile pixel game of the Wild West.

I'll build a single-page vanilla JS/HTML canvas game with pixel art, mobile-first. Western theme. Ideas:
- A vertical/landscape western shooter? Mobile-friendly controls (touch).
- Maybe a "duel" game: tap to draw and shoot outlaws popping up in a western town, with pixel art, parallax desert background, day/night.
- Or a side-scrolling "bounty hunter" with jump and shoot.

Interactive and beautiful pixel art. Best: a "Western Showdown" tap-shooter where you defend a saloon from bandits. Wave-based, with a hand-drawn canvas pixel art scene. Mobile portrait with big touch targets. Add juice: screen shake, muzzle flash, bullet tracers, dust particles, pixel font.

But "mobile game" likely wants touch controls. Maybe a character that moves left/right and shoots. A good design: portrait, player stands in front of saloon at bottom center. Enemies pop up from windows/cacti/barrels. Tap enemies to shoot. Add accuracy, combo, reload mechanic? Simple: tap-to-shoot with crosshair, bandits appear at 5 positions, shoot before timer. Health hearts. Waves. Ammo cylinder of 6 — tap to shoot, tap reload. That's engaging but maybe too simple.

Alternatively an endless runner "Pony Express" with tap to jump, shoot obstacles. Hmm.

I think tap-shooter with light strategy is best for mobile. Let me make it more interesting: bandits appear from behind cover with a wind-up (they aim, then fire). Tap them to shoot first. Some are civilians (don't shoot — penalty). Some hold dynamite. Reload via tapping revolver icon. Special "dead-eye" meter that slows time.

Visual design:
- Pixel canvas at low resolution (e.g., 240x400 internal) scaled up with nearest-neighbor for crisp pixels. Portrait mobile; responsive letterbox.
- Background: desert sunset gradient sky, sun, buttes silhouettes, cacti, town buildings (saloon), parallax dust drifting.
- Pixel art drawn procedurally with canvas rects to keep it crisp, no image assets needed. Add a nice color palette (warm oranges, deep purples, teal shadows).
- UI: pixel font via CSS (Google font "Press Start 2P" maybe offline?). Better use local pixel font via CSS with fallback; no network guarantee. Could use SVG-ish custom font? Use "monospace" with letter spacing — not great. Could craft bitmap font in canvas for HUD. I can implement a tiny 5x7 bitmap font for canvas text — nice retro look. But Google Fonts import might work offline? Avoid dependency; canvas bitmap font for headings.

Actually rendering UI in DOM with a pixel font from Google Fonts might fail offline. Let's draw everything on canvas with a custom bitmap font (5x7) to guarantee pixel aesthetic. I can define glyphs for A-Z, 0-9 and basic punctuation. That's a chunk but doable. Alternatively use CSS with `font-family: "Courier New"` styled — passable but not beautiful. Let's implement bitmap font; it's a nice touch.

Hmm, but also need Spanish/Portuguese? User wrote Portuguese; game text could be Portuguese ("FAROESTE", "TOQUE PARA ATIRAR"). The request says faroeste (Portuguese for western). I'll make the game UI in Portuguese. Pixel font then needs accents? Avoid accents, e.g. "MIRA", "MUNICAO" (no accent), or use accent glyphs optional. I'll use uppercase without accents mostly ("MUNICAO", "BALA", "RECARREGAR" - no accent needed). Some words: "SAQUE RAPIDO" (no accents), "BANDIDOS", "COMBO". Good.

Game design detail:

Title screen: "POEIRA & CHUMBO" (Dust & Lead) or "DUELO NO POEIRA". Scene with saloon, tumbleweed, title in big pixel letters, "TOQUE PARA COMECAR", best score.

Gameplay loop:
- 3 lanes? Let's do a "shooting gallery" across the width. Player revolver at bottom center. Bandits appear from behind 5-6 cover spots (barrels, windows, wagon). Each bandit rises with animation, has a timer indicator (ring or fuse). If you tap the bandit before its timer runs out, you shoot it (+points, combo). If the timer expires, they fire at you (-1 heart) with a muzzle flash and screen shake. Some enemies are "outlaws" (shoot) vs "civilians" (woman with hat? actually "cidadão" with white hat) — shooting them costs a heart or points. Dynamite-thrower: tap it twice? 
- Ammo: 6 bullets. Each shot consumes one, including misses. Tap the revolver cylinder at bottom to reload with animation (0.8s). Empty tap = click. This adds tension.
- Dead-eye meter fills with hits; when full, tap the eye button to slow time for 4 seconds and auto-highlight? Simpler: activates slow-motion (enemy timers slower) and unlimited ammo for its duration? Let's make "OLHO DE FALCAO": time slows 60% for 4s. Visual: sepia/blue tint, speed lines.
- Waves: 8 bandits per wave, increasing speed; every 5 waves a "boss" (bandido grande with 5 HP) maybe too complex. Keep endless with wave counter and difficulty ramp.
- Score + combo multiplier. Miss resets combo.

Rendering: internal resolution 270x480 (9:16). Scale factor computed by CSS canvas size. Use devicePixelRatio-aware? We'll set canvas width=270 height=480 and CSS scaled; image-rendering: pixelated. Good.

But drawing at 270x480 limits detail; that's fine for pixel art. Could use 360x640 for more detail with 2x scale. Pixel art chunks of 2-3px. Let's use 320x568 (iPhone 5 aspect) and draw with 2px pixel blocks? Actually canvas internal pixels are the pixel art units. Use 320x568, that's detailed enough.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Criar um jogo mobile de faroeste em pixel art, bonito, interativo e totalmente jogável.

## Requirements
- Construir o jogo agora, sem perguntas de esclarecimento; fazer suposições razoáveis e mencioná-las brevemente ao finalizar.
- Para verificações visuais, salvar JPEGs pequenos com viewport de até 1280 px e ler apenas o mais recente.

## Decisions
- Jogo em português chamado “Poeira & Chumbo”, feito com Canvas e arte/som procedural, sem downloads de recursos.
- Controles por toque e teclado; inclui ondas, bandidos, civis, recarga, modo “Olho de Falcão”, pontuação e recorde.

## Work State
### Completed
- Criados jogo, telas, controles, áudio procedural e layout responsivo.
- Servidor respondeu HTTP 200 em `http://localhost:3002/`; Chromium instalado e Playwright abriu a página.

### Active
- Verificação no navegador: a abertura reportou `Console: 1 errors, 0 warnings`; o erro ainda não foi investigado.
- Ainda não foi gerado nem lido um screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Investigar o erro no console do navegador e corrigir possíveis problemas de execução.
2. Testar fluxo do título ao jogo, interações, pausa, game over e reinício.
3. Salvar e ler o screenshot JPEG mais recente; depois resumir brevemente as suposições ao usuário.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: estrutura e entrada da página.
- `styles.css`: layout responsivo e apresentação mobile.
- `src/main.js`: lógica do jogo e entrada.
- `src/render.js`: composição dos quadros.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD e telas.
- `src/background.js`: cenário e paletas.
- `src/sprites.js`: personagens e ícones.
- `src/fx.js`: efeitos e projéteis.
- `src/audio.js`: áudio procedural.
- `src/font.js`: fonte bitmap.

## Important Context
- Última ação: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` abriu a página “Poeira & Chumbo — Duelo de Pixels” e reportou um erro de console; conferir o log associado no diretório de saída do Playwright.
- Não houve confirmação de commit ou push.

## Objective
- Criar um jogo mobile de faroeste em pixel art, bonito, interativo e totalmente jogável.

## Requirements
- Construir sem perguntas de esclarecimento; fazer suposições razoáveis e mencioná-las brevemente ao finalizar.
- Para verificações visuais, salvar JPEGs pequenos com viewport de até 1280 px e ler apenas o mais recente.

## Decisions
- Jogo em português chamado “Poeira & Chumbo”, feito com Canvas e arte/som procedural, sem downloads de recursos.
- Controles por toque e teclado; inclui ondas, bandidos, civis, recarga, modo “Olho de Falcão”, pontuação e recorde.

## Work State
### Completed
- Criados jogo, telas, controles, áudio procedural e layout responsivo.
- Servidor respondeu HTTP 200 em `http://localhost:3002/`; Chromium abriu a página.

### Active
- Verificar e corrigir o erro de console reportado ao abrir a página.
- Testar o fluxo do título ao jogo, interações, pausa, game over e reinício.
- Salvar e ler o screenshot JPEG mais recente.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Investigar o erro de console no log associado à saída do Playwright.
2. Corrigir possíveis problemas de execução e testar os fluxos principais.
3. Salvar e ler um screenshot JPEG recente; resumir brevemente as suposições ao finalizar.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: estrutura e entrada da página.
- `styles.css`: layout responsivo e apresentação mobile.
- `src/main.js`: lógica do jogo e entrada.
- `src/render.js`: composição dos quadros.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD e telas.
- `src/background.js`: cenário e paletas.
- `src/sprites.js`: personagens e ícones.
- `src/fx.js`: efeitos e projéteis.
- `src/audio.js`: áudio procedural.
- `src/font.js`: fonte bitmap.
